:: J U D G M E N T :
:
Petitioners filed Claim Petition U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/ for the death of M.Murugesh @ Murugeshan in road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as hereunder:
On 21.06.2021, at about 9.45 a.m., Murugesh M., was proceeding from Ibbluru towards fire station by riding TVS Jupiter Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA51EM 7488 slowly and cautiously on the correct side of the road.

When he was reached near fire station, one Container Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA05AF 0252 came from same direction with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and the driver of said vehicle lost control and went to wrong side of the road and dashed the aforesaid motor cycle from behind.
As a result of which, left side front wheel of the Container Lorry ran over the head of Murugesh M and he died on the spot due to severe grievous injuries.

sentences.text: The driver of the container lorry ran away from the spot.

The deceased Murugesh M.,
was taken to St. John's Hospital, Bangalore for postmortem.
Deceased was hale and healthy and he was aged about 46 years at the time of accident.
He was a Labour Contractor in building construction and earning Rs.50,000/ per month and in future he was earning more than Rs.1,00,000/ per month.
Petitioners are entirely depending on the earnings of the deceased and they have no any other source of income.
They were put to mental agony and untold misery due to untimely death of deceased.
The petitioners have spent Rs.2,00,000/ towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies of deceased.
The accident was occurred due to carelessness, rash and negligent driving of the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA05AF0252 by its driver.
The 1st respondent is the RC owner of offending Lorry and 2nd respondent is the insurer of the said vehicle.
Hence, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
With these averments petitioners prayed to allow the petition.
3. In response to the notice issued by the Tribunal, the 1st and 2nd respondents appeared through their counsels and filed written statements respectively.
4. The written statement averments of 1 st respondent are as here under:
The 1st respondent has denied the entire allegations made in the petition.
This respondent has denied the rash and negligent driving of the offending lorry by its driver.
Further denied the avocation, income and amount spent by the petitioners.
It is contended that, it is the R.C. owner of the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA05AF0252 and the said lorry was insured with the 2nd respondent and the Insurance Policy was valid at the time of accident.
Further contended that, the driver of aforesaid lorry was having valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
Further contended that, the accident took place due to negligence of the deceased, but the petitioners have created documents to file the petition.
If the petitioners have proved their claim, 2nd respondent is liable to pay compensation.
With these averments, the 1st respondent has prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. The written statement averments of 2 nd respondent are as here under:
Respondent No.2 has admitted the issuance of Insurance Policy with respect to vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA05AF0252 and its validity at the time of accident and contended that, the liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It is contended that, the driver of offending lorry had no valid and effective driving license to driver the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA05 AF0252 at the time of accident.

It is contended that owner of offended vehicle has entrusted his vehicle to the said driver by violating the policy conditions Further contended that, the owner of the offending vehicle has not complied the mandatory duty as per Section 134(c) of M.V.
Act.
The police have failed to comply the provisions of Sec.158(6) of M.V. Act.

sentences.text: ISSUE No.1 to 3: These issues are inter connected.
Hence, they have taken together for common discussion in order to avoid repetition.

10. It is the case of the petitioners that, on 21.06.2012 at about 9.45 a.m., deceased Murugesh M.,
was proceeding as a rider on the TVS Jupiter bearing Reg.No.KA51EM7488, at which point of time Container Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA05AF 0252 caused accident, due to impact, deceased Murugesh M., succumbed to injuries on the spot.
11. In order to prove the claim of petitioners, the petitioner No.2 was examined as P.W.1 by filing affidavit.

12. According to the respondent No.1, there is no fault from the side of offending container lorry.
The said lorry was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force.

13. Before going to discuss the issues, it is appropriate to say the admitted facts of the case.
There is no dispute with regard to death of Murugesh M., in the road traffic accident.

The respondent No.2 has not seriously disputed the relationship of petitioners with deceased Murugesh M.
14.
So, now the important question before this Tribunal is to find out whether the accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of offending vehicle or not ?
In order to answer these aspects, it is appropriate to take Ex.P.1, Ex.P.2, Ex.P.3, Ex.P.4, Ex.P.5, Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.19.
On careful perusal of these documents, it is clear that, criminal case was registered against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Apart from that, charge sheet was submitted against the driver of the offending vehicle as per Ex.P.19.

It is relevant to note that, though the respondent No.2 has contended that, accident was occurred due to the negligence of the deceased, however, in order to substantiate the same, the 1st respondent has not placed any material before this Tribunal.
Further, the 1st respondent has not endeavor to examine the driver of the offending vehicle.

Apart from that, as per Ex.P.6, C.C.
2673/2021 has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle.

Therefore, it is manifest that,
the materials placed on record by the petitioners is sufficient to believe that, the accident took place due to rash or negligent driving of driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA05AF0252.
Apart from that, the 2nd respondent has contended that, deceased was not wearing helmet and the driver of offending vehicle driving licence as on the date of accident.

At this juncture itself it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Dharwad Bench in M.F.A. 101144/2020 between Anand Vs. Arjun and Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka interpreted Sec.129 of IMV Act and held that, "non wearing of helmet is not a ground to deny the compensation".

sentences.text: Further, the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sudhir Kumar Rana Vs. Surinder Singh and Others held that, "mere non possessing of D.L. cannot be held to be guilty of contributory negligence.

sentences.text: To put it differently if a person drives a vehicle without a licence, he commits an offence.
The same by itself may not lead to a finding of negligence as regards the accident".
Further, on perusal of Ex.P.19, the police have not inserted the sections pertaining to the offending driver has not possessed D.L. at the time of accident.
Moreover, SPA holder of the 1st respondent has been examined as R.W.2.
He has produced driving licence of the driver of offending vehicle.
The said document marked as Ex.R.4.
Therefore, it is crystal clear that, as on the date of accident, driver of offending vehicle had possessed valid D.L. Hence, the contention of respondent No.2 holds no water.

15. At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

sentences.text: Age: Now, the next aspect is with regard to age of the deceased.
In the instant case, the respondent No.2 has disputed the age of the deceased.
According to the petitioners, the deceased was aged about 46 years.
P.W.1 was also deposed that, his father was aged about 46 years at the time of his death.
In order to substantiate the same, he has produced the notarized copy of D.L. and Aadhaar Card of deceased Murugesh, which are marked as Ex.P.10 and Ex.P.11.
On careful perusal of these documents, it reveals that, the date of birth of deceased is 01.01.1972.
The accident was occurred on 21.06.2021.
Therefore, age of the deceased is considered as 49 years at the time of accident.
17. Income of the deceased:
Respondent No.2 has disputed the avocation and income of deceased.
P.W.1 has deposed that, his father was a labour contractor in building construction under different employer and he was earning Rs.50,000/ per month.

However, to substantiate the income of the deceased, the P.W.1 has produced Ex.P.18, the work order, Ex.P.20, the bank account statement,
Ex.P.21, Ex.P.22, Ex.P.23 and Ex.P.25 i.e, the Income Tax Return Verification Forms for the assessment year 201314, 201415, 202021 and 201213 respectively.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has furnished the decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2023 ACJ 327, between Rupali Kailash Mamodu and Others Vs. Natinoal Insurance Company and Others and 2023 ACJ 637 between Anjali and Others Vs. Lokendra Rathod and Others.

sentences.text: In two decisions the Hon'ble Apex Court observed that, the High Court erred in taking average of last three years income.
Further, the Hon'ble Apex Court in another decision held that, Income Tax Return is a statutory document and as to be relied on to assess income fixed.
Admittedly on 21.06.2021, Murugesh was died in the road traffic accident.

Therefore, by relying on the judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court referred to above,
Ex.P.23 is the income tax returns has to be taken into consideration in order to ascertain the actual income of the deceased.
On careful perusal of Ex.P.23, the gross income of the deceased for the year 2021 is shown as Rs.1,25,100/.

Hence, the income of the deceased is considered as Rs.1,25,100/
per annum and Rs.10,425/ per month.

Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative,
Issue No.2 is answered in the Partly Affirmative and Issue No.3 is answered in the Affirmative.
18. ISSUE No.4:
This issue is with regard to entitlement of compensation.

According to the petition averments, petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the son, petitioner No.3 is the daughter petitioner No.4 is the father and petitioner No.5 is the mother of deceased Murugesh M.
The 1st petitioner has lost her husband.
2nd and 3rd petitioner have lost their loving father.
4th and 5th petitioners being the father and mother of deceased have lost their son at their old age.

Moreover,
the bond between the parents and children is an eternal.
Hence, petitioners Nos.1 to 5 are considered as dependents of deceased.
Keeping in view of the 5 dependents of deceased in the case on hand, 1/4th of the amount is to be deducted from total income toward his personal expenses.
19. Already this Tribunal has observed that, as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 49 years.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, held that "if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospects has to be taken into consideration while awarding compensation".

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is relevant to note that The Hon'ble Apex Court has provided the chart for the age of the deceased and percentage of future prospects as hereunder:
Kaveri Murugesan Alias Kaveramma vs Saniya Steel Corporation on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70642457/
7

entities.text: Kaveri Murugesan Alias Kaveramma vs Saniya Steel Corporation on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "If the deceased is self employed or fixed salary, his age below 40 years, future prospects is 40%".
"If the deceased between 40 to 50 years age, future prospects is 25%".
"If the deceased between 50 to 60 years age, future prospects is 10% and if the deceased more than 60 years, no addition as future prospects".
20. Admittedly, the petitioners have not produced any documents to show the income of deceased.
Hence, the deceased is not a permanent job holder and he is not a fixed salary person.
The deceased was aged about 49 years and therefore, additional income is added to the income towards future prospects.
In the instant case, the deceased was 49 years.
Hence, the future prospects of 25% is to be added to the income of deceased.
By applying the principles of above ruling, 25% of the income of Rs.10,425/ i.e, Rs.2,606.25/, which is rounded off to Rs.2,607/ is to be added to his monthly income.

By adding the said amount, monthly income of deceased would be Rs.13,032/ (i.e.,
Rs.10,425 + Rs.2,607/).
In this case petitioners Nos.1 to 5 are considered as dependents of deceased.
Keeping in view of the 5 dependents of deceased in the case on hand, 1/4th amount is to be deducted toward personal expenses of deceased.
After deducting 1/4 th from Rs.13,032/ the actual monthly income would be Rs.9,774/ (i.e, Rs.13,032 - Rs.3,258).

Then total income of the deceased per annum would be Rs.1,17,288/ (Rs.9,774 x 12)
21.
As the deceased was 49 years old at the time of death, the multiplier of 13 is applied, which is appropriate to age of deceased.
The normal compensation would then workout to be Rs.1,17,288 x 13 = Rs.15,24,744/ for loss of dependency.

22. The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others has laid down the guidelines with regard to awarding compensation towards loss of estate, funeral expenses and consortium.

sentences.text: The petitioners have contended that, they have spent Rs.2,00,000/ towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
In order to substantiate the same, they have not produced any documents.
Now the question before this Tribunal is whether petitioners Nos.2 to 5 are also entitled for consortium or not?
Admittedly, the 1st petitioner is the wife and she is entitled for spousal consortium.
Admittedly the petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are the major son and daughter of deceased.
Petitioner No.4 and 5 are the father and mother of deceased.
At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2018 (1) SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanuram @ Churu Ram and Others.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanuram @ Churu Ram and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court held that, the parents and children are having right to get the compensation under filial consortium.

It is relevant to note that, the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others Case, observed that, the conventional heads namely filial consortium, loss of estate, funeral expenses has to be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others Case
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the 1 st petitioner is entitled for Rs.44,000/ under the head of spousal consortium and petitioner Nos.2 to 5 are entitled for Rs.44,000/ each under the head of filial consortium.
Further, Rs.16,500/ is awarded for funeral expenses and also Rs.16,500/ is awarded towards loss of estate.

24.
Regarding liability and interest.
Driving License:

At the cost of repetition, SPA holder of respondent No.1 has examined as R.W.1 and produced driving licence of the driver of offending vehicle, which is marked as Ex.R.4 and it reveals that, the driver of offending vehicle was holding valid and effective D.L. as on the date of alleged accident.
Insurance Policy and liability:
Respondent No.1 the insurance company has not disputed the issuance of insurance policy with respect to offending vehicle.
Hence, it can be inferred that, the policy of the offending vehicle was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, the respondent No.1 shall pay compensation amount to the petitioners.
Interest:

In view of the decision reported in MFA NO:
301312019 dtd, 12.5.2020, rate of interest on the compensation amount is awarded at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.
Accordingly, this Tribunal is answered Point No.4 in Partly Affirmative.
25. POINT No.5:.
In view of discussion made above, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following.

:ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the Petition.

Petitioners are awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs.17,77,744/ (Rupees Seventeen Lakhs, Seventy Seven Thousand Seven Hundred and Forty Four Only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the court.

:: J U D G M E N T :
:
Petitioners filed Claim Petition U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/ for the death of M.Murugesh @ Murugeshan in road traffic accident.
opennyai_summary.facts:
He was a Labour Contractor in building construction and earning Rs.50,000/ per month and in future he was earning more than Rs.1,00,000/ per month.
It is contended that, the driver of offending lorry had no valid and effective driving license to driver the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA05 AF0252 at the time of accident.
It is contended that owner of offended vehicle has entrusted his vehicle to the said driver by violating the policy conditions Further contended that, the owner of the offending vehicle has not complied the mandatory duty as per Section 134(c) of M.V.
Act.
The police have failed to comply the provisions of Sec.158(6) of M.V. Act.

3 nd respondent has age, avocation and income of the deceased, rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
It is contended the driver of offending vehicle was driven the vehicle slowly and cautiously on the correct side of the road.
The accident was occurred due to rash or negligence on the part of deceased, who was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA51EM7488 without wearing helmet.
Hence, the owner and insurer of motor cycle are necessary parties to the case.
opennyai_summary.arguments: It is contended that, the claim made by the petitioners is excessive and exorbitant.
opennyai_summary.issue:
: I S S U E S:
1.Whether petitioners proves that Murugesh alias Murugeshan was died on 21.06.2021 due to the injuries sustained in the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of driver of container lorry vehicle bearing Registration No.KA05 AF 0252 as stated in the petition?
2.Whether petitioners prove the age and income of the deceased?
 3.Whether the Respondent No.1 proves that,
 insurance company is liable to pay  compensation?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The said lorry was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force.
Hence, if the Tribunal come to the conclusion that, there is a fault on the driver of container lorry, insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.
Further, the 1st respondent has not endeavor to examine the driver of the offending vehicle.
Apart from that, as per Ex.P.6, C.C.
2673/2021 has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle.
Therefore, it is manifest that,
the materials placed on record by the petitioners is sufficient to believe that, the accident took place due to rash or negligent driving of driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA05AF0252.
Apart from that, the 2nd respondent has contended that, deceased was not wearing helmet and the driver of offending vehicle driving licence as on the date of accident.
At this juncture itself it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Dharwad Bench in M.F.A. 101144/2020 between Anand Vs. Arjun and Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka interpreted Sec.129 of IMV Act and held that, "non wearing of helmet is not a ground to deny the compensation".
He has produced driving licence of the driver of offending vehicle.
Therefore, it is crystal clear that, as on the date of accident, driver of offending vehicle had possessed valid D.L. Hence, the contention of respondent No.2 holds no water.
15. At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

6 16.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has furnished the decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2023 ACJ 327, between Rupali Kailash Mamodu and Others Vs. Natinoal Insurance Company and Others and 2023 ACJ 637 between Anjali and Others Vs. Lokendra Rathod and Others.
On careful perusal of Ex.P.23, the gross income of the deceased for the year 2021 is shown as Rs.1,25,100/.
4th and 5th petitioners being the father and mother of deceased have lost their son at their old age.
Moreover,
the bond between the parents and children is an eternal.
Hence, petitioners Nos.1 to 5 are considered as dependents of deceased.
Keeping in view of the 5 dependents of deceased in the case on hand, 1/4th of the amount is to be deducted from total income toward his personal expenses.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, held that "if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospects has to be taken into consideration while awarding compensation".
20. Admittedly, the petitioners have not produced any documents to show the income of deceased.
Hence, the deceased is not a permanent job holder and he is not a fixed salary person.
The deceased was aged about 49 years and therefore, additional income is added to the income towards future prospects.
In the instant case, the deceased was 49 years.
Hence, the future prospects of 25% is to be added to the income of deceased.
By applying the principles of above ruling, 25% of the income of Rs.10,425/ i.e, Rs.2,606.25/, which is rounded off to Rs.2,607/ is to be added to his monthly income.
22. The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others has laid down the guidelines with regard to awarding compensation towards loss of estate, funeral expenses and consortium.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, the 1 st petitioner is entitled for Rs.44,000/ under the head of spousal consortium and petitioner Nos.2 to 5 are entitled for Rs.44,000/ each under the head of filial consortium.
Further, Rs.16,500/ is awarded for funeral expenses and also Rs.16,500/ is awarded towards loss of estate.
Hence, the respondent No.1 shall pay compensation amount to the petitioners.
In view of the decision reported in MFA NO:

Accordingly, this Tribunal is answered Point No.4 in Partly Affirmative.
